predecessors.note: 'In the year of 660, Ungjin Commandery is a administrative subdivision set up.' The central government sat at Sabi castle (Buyeo County, Chungcheong).

land.text: Baekje's last Cliopatria outline (656..660): 'created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province after its defeat by a joint Silla-Tang alliance'

successors.note: 'Ungjin Commandery was occupied by Silla'; the Silla-Tang War page: 'In 671, Silla drove Tang forces out of most of Baekje's former territory'. The Tang command then moved to Geonan castle (Yingkou, Liaoning) under the Protectorate General to Pacify the East.

capitals.name: Sabi castle (Buyeo, also called Goma castle)
capitals.note: 'The central government was at Sabi castle (Buyeo County, Chungcheong). Sabi is also called Goma castle, and Ungjin is listed as the administrative center.' The Buyeo place of the gazetteer.

correction.text: Baekje's last Cliopatria outline (656..660): 'created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province after its defeat by a joint Silla-Tang alliance'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Ungjin row; its Baekje row ends 660 and Silla's shape grows later). The page gives the Tang's seven commanderies in Baekje land (Ungjin, Mahan, Dongmyeong, Deongan, Daemang, Gimnan, Angdong) and no boundaries or area. The Baekje restoration movement held Juryu (Seocheon) 660-663, inside this outline, so a renderer should let the rebel patch win there; Silla's own gains in the same land from 660 are in the silla dossier (jk-02-c).

region.text: Baekje's last Cliopatria outline (656..660): 'created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province after its defeat by a joint Silla-Tang alliance'

ledger.note: 660: the Tang set up the Ungjin Commandery on conquered Baekje. The lead: 'existed between 660 and 671' and 'was created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province after its defeat by a joint Silla-Tang alliance'. The page names no month; the fall of Sabi is in the baekje dossier (9 July 660 Hwangsanbeol).

region.text: Baekje's last Cliopatria outline (656..660): 'created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province after its defeat by a joint Silla-Tang alliance'

ledger.note: July 670: Silla attacks Ungjin. 'Silla rebelled and attached [attacked] Ungjin Commandery in July, 670. 82 castle have been surrendered.' Xue Rengui was sent to fight Silla and 'failed'.

region.text: Baekje's last Cliopatria outline (656..660): 'created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province after its defeat by a joint Silla-Tang alliance'

ledger.note: 671: Silla takes Baekje's former land from the Tang. 'In 671, Silla drove Tang forces out of most of Baekje's former territory' (Silla-Tang War page); the Ungjin page: 'Ungjin Commandery was occupied by Silla', without a year beyond the 660-671 span. The Tang command moved to Geonan castle (Yingkou).

region.text: Baekje's last Cliopatria outline (656..660): 'created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province after its defeat by a joint Silla-Tang alliance'

ledger.note: 671: the fighting over the Ungjin land ends in Silla's favour.

region.text: Baekje's last Cliopatria outline (656..660): 'created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province after its defeat by a joint Silla-Tang alliance'

ledger.note: 671: Ungjin Commandery ends. Silla later set up its own Ungjin Territorial Area Command in 686 (renamed Ungcheon 757, Gongju 940).

wars.name: Baekje restoration movement

zones.text: Juryu (Churyu), the restoration's headquarters 'in modern Seocheon County': by 662 the 'area of control was confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity'

wars.outcome: Dochim and Buyeo Boksin raise Baekje with Buyeo Pung from Japan; confined to Juryu by 662; the Tang-Silla forces win the Battle of Baekgang (27-28 August 663 lunar; 4-5 October 663 Julian) and crush it.
wars.note: Juryu was under Silla siege in 663; Tang sent 7,000 soldiers and 170 ships against the Yamato navy.

wars.name: Silla-Tang War (Ungjin phase)

zones.text: Baekje's last Cliopatria outline (656..660): 'created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province after its defeat by a joint Silla-Tang alliance'

wars.outcome: Silla attacks Ungjin in July 670 (82 castles surrender) and drives the Tang out of most of Baekje's former land in 671.

certainty.note: Occupation lines moved with the Baekje restoration (660-663) and the Silla attack (670-671); the page gives no boundaries.

notes: Colony (Tang occupation) in Baekje's land, 11 years. The Ungjin page is a poor translation (e.g. 'attached' for 'attacked'; 'Deongan' for the commandery usually spelled Deokan) and gives no month for the founding or the end. The Baekje dossier (jk-02-b) ends in 660 and treats the Tang-controlled revival as a war only: the restoration movement is a rebel dossier of this batch (baekje-restoration-movement). The Silla-Tang War page gives the 671 expulsion; the tang-dynasty example puts the Silla war's contest zone at Baekje (core), Hwanghae and Gyeonggi from 670 and the loss in 676 (different from the 671 here: Silla held the Baekje land from 671 and the Taedong line from 676). The region of the Tang commanderies is Chungcheong only on the page; Jeolla is assumed to follow.
